status: planned: generated by tools/ursaluna_cave.py and audited offline by tools/ursaluna_cave_audit.py on 2026-10-02; not applied to any world
request: the owner, 2026-10-02, verbatim: "make an ursuluna cave at 1504 164 1414, dig a solid size caev for a large ursuluna, have teddiursa spawn on the outskirt and have an npc one players can talk to"

site.mouth_why: the owner's coordinate. tools/ground.py reads y162 there (heightmap 162.19), so the owner's y164 is a standing eye-line two blocks up, not the floor: the cave floor is the ground at the mouth, and a player walks in without a step. Highwire's nearest building (gym3_house_03, (1661, 1410)) is 157 blocks east; Route 3 ends at Highwire's centre (1688, 1410) coming up from the south-east, and Route 4 leaves it eastward.
site.axis_why: into the hill. The mouth sits on the south-east foot of a ridge that climbs north-west to y200 at (1450, 1350) and y217 at (1432, 1294) (tools/ground.py, sampled every 6 blocks). Due west the ground only reaches y174 before falling again, and due north y174: neither covers a chamber. North-west it rises 162 -> 180 in 25 blocks and to y194 over the chamber, so the chamber is under 13+ blocks of hill. The mouth therefore opens to the south-east, 45 degrees off the line to Highwire (due east), facing the last stretch of Route 3.

cave.margin_why: the legendary chambers' shell_margin (data/legendaries.json defaults, WATER_BUILD_PLAN 4.5 audit 1): at least 4 blocks of rock round every void past the mouth, guaranteed by construction because the shell is filled solid before the void is cut.
cave.keep_natural_top_why: the shell never writes into the top two blocks of any column, so the grass and the dirt under it stay the terrain's own and the hill's surface is never raised or re-skinned.
cave.open_mouth_until_why: the mouth is a cut and then an overhang, not a door. The passage's top block is y170 and tools/ground.py reads the crown line (s:y) 0:162 8:167 13:170 14:171 17:173 20:175 22:177: so s 0-13 is a cut open to the sky, the roof begins at s 14 (the arch, about (1494, 1404)), and its roof is the hillside's own grass and dirt until the ground stands margin + 1 over it at s 20. The slope also falls away sideways there: the audit's seal check, which looks margin blocks in every direction and not only up, first holds at s 22 (at 21 one block of open air at (1484, 174, 1404) is within 4 of the passage). 22 is that measured boundary, not a padded one; past it every carved block has margin + 1 blocks of ground over it and margin blocks of rock round it.

passage.why: a half-elliptical bore 9 wide at the floor and 8 high at the crown, level at the mouth's ground (y162) all the way in: wide and tall enough that the opening reads as a bear's den from the slope below, and level so nothing has to be climbed. It overlaps the chamber by 3 blocks so the two join without a lip.

chamber.why: a half-ellipsoid hall 39 blocks long, 29 wide and 17 high over a flat floor, centred 60 blocks in. Sized from the model, not guessed: the Ursaluna stands 8 by 8 by at most 10.3 blocks at scale 2 (ursaluna.model below), so the den end of the hall, 11 blocks from the centre where the bear lies, still has 23 blocks of width at the floor and 14 of height over it (tools/ursaluna_cave.py --report): the bear fills the den without touching it, and the hall in front is twice its size again.

den.why: a barrier curtain across the whole hall, 2 blocks thick (thick enough that no face-adjacent path crosses a band on a diagonal axis), 8 blocks before the bear. Barriers are invisible and solid: the bear is seen through them, and a sword, an arrow or a thrown ball stops at them. That is the sleeping Celebi's protection (data/sapling_celebi.json shell_why), because Cobblemon ignores Invulnerable and a sword killed the Celebi in three hits (EXP-023).

cave.lanterns_why: hanging lanterns under the roof (docs/STATE.md, 'Places are lit as towns': lanterns, never light blocks), each [s, p]: s along the axis from the mouth, p across it. Three down the passage (the first just inside the arch: s 0-13 is an open cut with no roof to hang from), five over the hall, one in the den over the bear so it is seen.
cave.blocks_why: vanilla only, and none of them is a spawn-conditioning block in data/spawn_blocks.json, so the cave adds no pack spawns. BUILD_PALETTE.md lists the decoration providers and names no cave stone; the shell is the stone the hill is made of.

ursaluna.level_why: the top of the_tri_peaks band (24-35, data/spawns.json subregions) that the cave is in, and gym 4's ace level (data/trainers.json generation_contract gym_ace_levels[3] = 35), which is the RCT cap tier a player reaches when gym 3 is beaten (cap = the next trainers' highest level, docs/research/notes/level-cap-catch-block.md). It is the same level and the same 3-badge tier as Mesprit (data/legendaries.json). It does not matter yet: the bear is asleep and Unbattleable; it matters the day the owner decides it wakes.
ursaluna.yaw_why: facing south-east, back along the axis toward the mouth and the visitor: Minecraft yaw 0 faces +z, -90 faces +x, so -45 faces (+x, +z).
ursaluna.scale_why: 'large' is the scale_modifier property: Cobblemon 1.8.0's PokemonProperties parses scale_modifier= (strings in PokemonProperties and PokemonProperties$Companion, Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar) and Pokemon.getEffectiveScale returns the scale modifier for a non-alpha Pokemon past baby age (javap of Pokemon.class). It is saved as ScaleModifier, so a restart keeps it. NOT alpha=true, which also exists: getAlphaScaleMultiplier fixes an alpha's scale at 1.1 + 0.8 * 0.5^max(hitbox) = 1.3 for Ursaluna's 2.0 hitbox and ignores scale_modifier, and an alpha brings the alpha battle boost and drops, which are balance, not size. NEEDS AN IN-GAME CHECK: that the summoned bear is twice normal size (the property is applied after the random intrinsic scale is rolled, which the bytecode suggests but no run has shown).
ursaluna.nbt_why: the sleeping Celebi's flags exactly (data/sapling_celebi.json nbt, EXP-023: each proved to hold across a restart). Ursaluna's own poser has a SLEEP pose (posers/0901_ursaluna/ursaluna.json 'sleep', animation.ursaluna.sleep), so the pose has something to play.
ursaluna.encounter_why: asleep and unbattleable, not a fight. Nothing in the request asks for a battle, and a placed Pokemon that is knocked out is gone for the whole group until the next re-application, so making it a fight is a decision for the owner, not for a carve. The legendaries' gated wake (tools/legendaries.py open/close: a badge gate on a barrier, the AWAKE merge) is the established way to make it one, and the level above is already set for it.

keeper.why: the Celebi keeper's shape (tools/sapling_celebi.py celebi/keep): every 2 s while a player is within 48 blocks of the den, remove a second tagged bear if a load race made one and put it back on its spot if anything moved it. It cannot summon a missing one (Cobblemon's spawn command does nothing in a plainly parsed function); the re-application does that.

model.cube_bounds_source: assets/cobblemon/bedrock/pokemon/models/0901_ursaluna/ursaluna.geo.json: the union of every cube's origin and size, ignoring bone rotation (x -28..36 px, y -40.5..42 px, z -38.5..27.8 px): an over-estimate, so a chamber sized to it is safe
model.assumed: the rendered model scales with the effective scale as the hitbox does; at 2.0 the bear is about 8 wide, 8.3 long and at most 10.3 tall, with a 3.6 by 4.0 hitbox

teddiursa.why: the established pattern: a natural Habitat Block (data/habitat_blocks.json, placed by tools/habitat_blocks.py with every other block) whose ReplaceSpawns takes over the ambient pool within its range, and a Habitat pool authored in data/spawns.json (compiled by tools/compile_spawns.py). The pool is Teddiursa alone, 24-29: inside the_tri_peaks band (24-35) and below level 30, where Teddiursa evolves (species data), so no wild Teddiursa is older than its own evolution.

npc.at_why: 8 blocks across the axis from the mouth on the Highwire side and 4 out from it (s=-4, p=8), on the slope beside the opening, standing one above the heightmap ground (tools/ground.py: y162): the first thing a player coming from Highwire reaches, outside every carved block and every column the cave writes. Placed over RCON by spawnnpcat after a restart (tools/reapply.py's "npc" action, as R9F, R17 and R17F place theirs); the class ships in cobblers_dialogue, compiled from data/dialogue.json.
